title: Comparing Quantities
description: Class 7 IMO — Comparing Quantities: percentage conversions and calculations, profit and loss with CP and SP, simple interest, and basic discount and GST.

topics.title: Percentage
topics.concept:
Percent means per hundred (out of 100). Percent problems appear in everyday life as discounts, taxes, and markups.

Problem TypeFormula
DiscountDiscount = Original Price x Discount%. Sale Price = Original - Discount
TaxTax = Price x Tax%. Total = Price + Tax
MarkupMarkup = Cost x Markup%. Selling Price = Cost + Markup
Percent Increase(New - Old) / Old x 100%
Percent Decrease(Old - New) / Old x 100%

Always convert percent to decimal first: 25% = 0.25

PERCENT CHANGE NUMBER LINE:

0%              100%            150%            200%
|----------------|----------------|----------------|
Original        Double           1.5x            2x

CONVERT % TO DECIMAL:
  25% = 25/100 = 0.25
  8%  = 8/100  = 0.08
  50% = 50/100 = 0.50

examples.problem: 25% of a number is 50. Find the number.
A $80 shirt is 25% off. What is the sale price?
A $50 meal has 8% tax. What is the total bill?
A town's population grew from 2,000 to 2,500. What is the percent increase?

recap: Percentage of a number: multiply by the percentage as a fraction.
Find the whole: divide the part by the percentage and multiply by 100.
Original price = Sale price / (1 - discount rate)

topics.title: Profit, Loss, CP & SP
topics.concept: The cost price (CP) is what an item costs and the selling price (SP) is what it sells for. Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP. The percentages are found on the CP: profit% = (profit ÷ CP) × 100.
recap: Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP.
Profit% and loss% are calculated on the CP.

quiz.q: CP = ₹100, SP = ₹130. What is the profit%?

topics.title: Simple Interest, Discount & GST
topics.concept: Simple interest is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, and the amount is P + SI. A discount is a percentage off the marked price. GST is a tax added on, such as 18% GST adding ₹18 on every ₹100.

examples.problem: Find the SI on ₹1000 at 5% for 2 years and the amount.
A ₹500 item has a 10% discount. What do you pay?

recap: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; amount = P + SI.
Discount reduces the price; GST adds tax on.
